enclosure.top_mount_load_path: Directly into full-height tray posts; removable cover is bypassed
enclosure.lid_screw: M3x20 socket, recessed 0.3 mm below mounting face

spring_carrier.design: two opposed leaves per lower bearing carrier
spring_carrier.method: Prescribed displacement with level carrier; symmetric linear beam proxy, not finite element analysis. Actual tilt, stiffness, creep and fatigue require print testing. STL relaxed; STEP/viewer deflected. No mechanical stop.

root_relief.shape: semicircular caps tangent to straight slot walls

insertion_side: right/output side, plain left end first
method: All assembled pairs. Changed enclosure and enclosure-fastener relative motion sampled <=0.5 mm. Mechanism pairs checked at 1% explosion intervals, every stage boundary/midpoint and bearing-release transitions at 0.5 mm spacing; all moving parts checked at 41 travel positions. Exact verified box coverage rejects empty enclosure and rack regions; lid screw removal is proven with continuous swept outer envelopes. Equal-phase mesh intersections are reused only inside an exactly verified periodic rack/pinion region. Same tracks drive viewer. Nominal tooth profile checked separately.

intentional_contacts.reason: Intentional heat-set knurl/pilot interference; plastic displaced during installation

limits: 2.3 mm default spring deflection is an aggressive physical prototype. Force, elastic recovery and fatigue require testing in the chosen print material.
Sampled rigid geometry, not continuous swept-volume proof or a physical fit test.
Oversized teeth require elastic deflection. No load, backlash or fatigue rating.
The plain insertion end has no axial hard stop; enforce software travel limits.
Viewer chassis uses exact CAD shape samples at one twelfth of the spring preload; bearing translations follow the CAD tracks continuously.

Pinion is free to turn during rack insertion. Remove front and rear angled axles in sequence. Spring carrier supplies passive preload; force, creep and fatigue have not been measured. STL is unloaded; STEP is assembled and deflected.
